title: Control evidence orchestration: RBAC, audit schema & SIEM export — gap analysis + auditor FAQ
content:
Executive summary:

This working playbook outlines how RBAC v2, the canonical audit-log schema, and our SIEM export pipeline map to SOC 2 and ISO 27001 control areas, identifies gaps for the upcoming external audit, and provides short, auditable answers and evidence pointers for common auditor questions. Intended audience: security/compliance, infra/serving-runtime, and SRE owners who will supply evidence or implement remediations.

Scope and assumptions:
- Scope: Hosted API + Dedicated control plane + Private control plane logging surfaces.
- Includes: RBAC v2 role model and assignment records, auth/audit-log event stream, SIEM export snapshot and retention, evidence automation pipeline (ingest -> sign -> store -> ticket attach).
- Excludes: application-level business logs (handled by product teams) unless explicitly configured to forward.

Control mapping (high level):
- ISO 27001: A.9 Access control -> RBAC enforcement, privileged role lifecycle, periodic review evidence.
- ISO 27001: A.12 Operations -> Audit logging, log protection, backup and retention.
- ISO 27001: A.8 Asset control -> inventory of logging endpoints and collectors.
- SOC 2 (Security + Confidentiality): logical access controls, change control for role definitions, detection and monitoring via SIEM, evidence of alerting and incident handling.

Canonical audit-log schema (single-line description + required fields for exports):
- Format: newline-delimited JSON events (ndjson) for SIEM ingestion and snapshotting. Each event must include the following canonical fields: timestamp, event_id, actor_id, actor_email, actor_role_snapshot, action, target_type, target_id, outcome, ip_address, user_agent, region, auth_method, request_id, request_path, service_name, duration_ms, kv_cache_hit (if applicable), model_variant (if inference request), tenant_id, correlator_id (trace id), signature (signed HMAC of event payload).

Example event (ndjson):
{"timestamp":"2024-11-01T14:23:12.123Z","event_id":"evt_01Hxyz","actor_id":"u_1092","actor_email":"eng+alice@redwood.com","actor_role_snapshot":"roles:[platform-admin,model-onboarder]","action":"model.create","target_type":"model","target_id":"m_7b4","outcome":"success","ip_address":"54.83.2.11","user_agent":"redwood-cli/1.2.0","region":"us-west-2","auth_method":"oidc","request_id":"req_9a2","request_path":"/v1/models","service_name":"model-registry","duration_ms":123,"kv_cache_hit":false,"model_variant":"llama-2-13b-8bit","tenant_id":"acct_77","correlator_id":"trace-4f3","signature":"hmac_sha256:base64sig=="}

Notes on schema choices and why they matter:
- actor_role_snapshot: capture role(s) at time of event to prove who had access when action occurred (required for access control evidence).
- signature: HMAC of canonical serialized JSON with a rotating signing key (see evidence automation) to prove tamper-resistance between snapshot intervals.
- correlator_id + request_id: both help link multi-service spans to a single operation; required for investigations.
- model_variant, kv_cache_hit: domain-specific fields relevant to inference-related control mapping (shows resource variant used and caching behaviors).

Evidence automation pipeline (high level):
1) Ingest: services emit ndjson to central logging ingestion cluster (kinesis/pubsub).
2) Normalize: schema normalizer enriches events (resolve actor_id->email, add actor_role_snapshot from RBAC service snapshot).
3) Sign & seal: batch signer computes HMAC per-event and rolling Merkle snapshot per-hour and writes signatures to an append-only evidence bucket.
4) Export: SIEM export job converts hourly ndjson batches to the SIEM-compatible index format and pushes to SIEM (secure channel).
5) Snapshot retention & archive: daily snapshots (signed) are retained in cold storage for 2 years (configurable per contract).
6) Evidence linking: automation attaches snapshot IDs and sample event pointers to Jira incident/ticket for auditor access.

RBAC v2 specifics (what auditors will look for):
- Role model: canonical roles (platform-admin, infra-operator, svc-account, model-onboarder, app-developer, customer-support).
- Role assignment records are immutable (assignment events logged) and include: assignee_id, grantor_id, grant_time, grant_id, grant_reason, expiration (optional), review_cycle.
- Privileged role policies: MFA requirement, IP allow-lists for session initiation, mandatory just-in-time (JIT) elevation tracked via temporality tokens.
- Periodic review workflow: quarterly automated reminders; evidence stored as review artifacts with diff of assignments.

Gap analysis (current state -> gap -> risk -> proposed remediations):
- Gap 1: actor_role_snapshot not yet populated for ~10% of events emitted by legacy ingestion agents.
  - Risk: can't prove role membership at time of action for those events.
  - Remediation: deploy normalizer patch (PR#906) and replay missed events from retrospective audit log buffer; owner: Connor Lee; ETA: 3 weeks; Evidence: patch PR, normalization run logs, replay manifest.
- Gap 2: Event-level HMAC signing implemented but per-hour Merkle snapshots not yet automated; manual snapshotting done weekly during compliance run.
  - Risk: longer window where tamper detection is weaker; increases auditor friction.
  - Remediation: automate hourly Merkle snapshot job and integrate with evidence bucket lifecycle; owner: Priya Nair; ETA: 4 weeks; Evidence: job definition, successful runs, signed snapshot files.
- Gap 3: SIEM export mapping lacks tenant_id normalization for Dedicated deployments outside primary region.
  - Risk: multi-tenant evidence mixing could hinder scope boundaries.
  - Remediation: extend export transform to normalize tenant_id and include deployment_region in every exported event; owner: Omar Reyes; ETA: 2 sprints; Evidence: export schema versioned notes, SIEM index sample.
- Gap 4: Role assignment historic snapshots retention is 90 days for svc-account grants; ISO requires evidence of privileged grants for longer depending on contract (up to 2 years).
  - Risk: inability to show long-lived privileged assignments to auditors.
  - Remediation: increase retention of role assignment snapshots for privileged roles to 2 years; add lifecycle policy; owner: Security Ops; ETA: 6 weeks; Evidence: retention policy change, bucket logs.

Prioritization matrix (short):
- P0 (audit-blocking): Gap 1, Gap 2.
- P1: Gap 4.
- P2: Gap 3.

Evidence checklist to attach for auditor requests (by control):
- Access control (ISO A.9 / SOC 2 access): role catalog export, role assignment event stream (signed ndjson), proof of periodic review (review artifacts).
- Logging & monitoring (ISO A.12 / SOC 2 monitoring): sample signed ndjson export for selected date range, SIEM ingestion confirmation, alert runbooks for high-severity detections.
- Change control for RBAC (SOC 2): PR history for role model changes, approval workflow screenshots, deployment manifests (k8s apply).
- Evidence of tamper-resistance: signer key rotation policy, signed Merkle snapshot files, evidence-bucket ACLs and immutability settings.

Typical auditor Q&A with suggested responses (copy/paste friendly):
- Q: How do you ensure the logged role membership corresponds to the time of the action?
  A: Our normalizer resolves actor_id to an actor_role_snapshot at ingestion time by querying the RBAC v2 snapshot service. The actor_role_snapshot field is embedded in the event and signed. We retain assignment history so snapshots are reproducible. Evidence: signed events + RBAC snapshot manifests for the relevant timestamps.

- Q: Can logs be altered after they are written?
  A: Events are HMAC-signed on ingest using per-region signing keys. Hourly Merkle snapshots are computed and the top-level snapshot signatures are stored in an append-only evidence bucket with immutability turned on. We maintain key rotation logs and KMS audit entries for signing operations.

- Q: How do you separate customer tenant data in SIEM exports?
  A: Exports include a normalized tenant_id field and deployment_region. Dedicated deployments are flagged, and export transforms tag events with a tenancy_scope field. We provide auditors with tenant-scoped snapshots on request.

- Q: Where is RBAC change history kept and how long?
  A: All role model changes are tracked in Git (PRs) and the resulting applied manifests are stored along with an immutable assignment-event stream. Privileged role assignment snapshots are retained for two years per our new retention policy; other assignments have 90-day retention by default.

- Q: How quickly can you produce evidence for a given incident window (e.g., last 30 days)?
  A: For signed ndjson events we can produce a tenant-scoped export for the required window within 24 hours; for cross-region or archival retrieval (older than 90 days) expect 3–5 business days depending on cold-storage retrieval. Evidence requests are tracked in Jira (SEC-requests) and linked to signed snapshot manifests.

Operational runbook snippets (for SREs to produce auditor packet):
1) Run the export job with parameters: start_ts, end_ts, tenant_id, include_signed=true.
2) Verify hash: run verify_signatures --manifest <manifest> against exported batch.
3) Produce artifacts: sample_event.ndjson (first 1000 events), manifest.json (signed), role_snapshot_export.csv, retention-policy.txt.
4) Attach artifacts to Jira ticket and tag compliance@redwood.com.

Appendix: quick reference of artifacts and where to find them:
- Signed event batches: s3://evidence-bucket/signed-events/YYYY/MM/DD/
- Merkle snapshots: s3://evidence-bucket/snapshots/YYYY/MM/DD/hourly-merkle.json.sig
- RBAC snapshots: s3://rbac-snapshots/role-snapshots/YYYY-MM-DDT*.json
- SIEM export index sample: attached to confluence:SECOPS-LOGS-PIPELINE (index-v1.4)

Open questions / decisions to finalize before audit:
- Retention length for non-privileged role assignment events (propose 1 year vs current 90 days).
- Formal sign-off on archive retrieval SLA for auditors (propose 3 business days).
- Add tenant-scoped SIEM export runbook for Dedicated customers (owner: Omar).

Action items (owner, ETA):
- Connor Lee: deploy normalizer patch and replay buffer (ETA: 3 weeks).
- Priya Nair: automate hourly Merkle snapshots and update evidence bucket lifecycle (ETA: 4 weeks).
- Omar Reyes: add tenant normalization to SIEM export and provide sample index (ETA: 2 sprints).
- Security Ops: update retention policy for privileged role snapshots to 2 years and publish change (ETA: 6 weeks).

This document is a working playbook: comments requested from infra, serving-runtime, and product security teams. Use the linked artifacts above for technical proofs and attach any additional evidence to the SEC-requests Jira queue.
